text:
Emma: heads up — hitting a weird bug where request IDs (x-request-id) set by our middleware are not making it to downstream services when using the async Python SDK + create_task. Tracing/otel shows gaps.
Raj: can you paste a tiny repro? which sdk version? :eyes:
Emma: using redwood-sdk==0.12.3, python 3.11. repro below. it only happens when we spawn background tasks.
Emma: ```python
import asyncio
from redwood import AsyncClient

client = AsyncClient(api_key=...),

async def do_call():
    resp = await client.responses.create(model="gpt-mini", input="hi")
    print(resp.output)

async def main():
    # we set request id in middleware earlier (contextvar)
    asyncio.create_task(do_call())
    await asyncio.sleep(0.5)

asyncio.run(main())
```
Raj: ok. this smells like contextvars not being preserved across create_task when using threadpool or run_in_executor. are you using any sync wrappers?
Emma: we don't explicitly run anything in a threadpool, just the SDK internals streaming code. if i await the call directly it works. create_task loses the header.
Ben: can you confirm header name? our otel and logging also rely on `x-request-id`.
Emma: yes header is `x-request-id`. middleware sets it from a contextvar at the start of the request.
Maria: interesting — we recently changed the async client to use a background thread for streaming reads on some platforms to avoid event-loop starvation. that could explain contextvar loss.
Raj: middleware ordering matters too. if the retry wrapper re-dispatches work in a different loop/worker it could drop context.
Ben: quick workaround — pass explicit headers into the client call: `await client.responses.create(..., headers={"x-request-id": req_id})` until we fix.
Emma: confirmed workaround works. but that breaks the clean middleware propagation goal for customers. also typing: typed clients don't surface `headers` kw in stubbed types in 0.12.x; had to `# type: ignore`.
Maria: ok plan: 1) revert the background thread in async streaming path or use contextvars.copy_context when scheduling; 2) add a typed optional `headers` kw to the async signatures (parity with sync); 3) add an integration test exercising create_task + otel middleware.
Ben: i'll open a PR for (2) and tests. assigning to me. PR will include a small sample app in examples/devex/requestid_background_task.py and a note in the changelog. expected PR: #9421. :rocket:
CI-Bot: build 9421 started — running unit + integration tests
Ops-Bot: FYI, I'm logging this as DX-537 (observability: python async request-id propagation) for backlog tracking.
Raj: nice. one more: let's add a tiny snippet in the python quickstart showing `contextvars.copy_context().run(asyncio.create_task, ...)` as a defensive pattern, or better, a wrapper helper in devex utils.
Emma: thanks all. flakiness repro was blocking a customer demo, so will ship hotfix if CI for #9421 looks good. :thumbsup:
CI-Bot: build 9421 passed — integration tests include new request-id scenario.
Emma: awesome. can we also add a short note in onboarding sample-apps about OTEL middleware + async caveats? new hires always trip on this.
Ben: added to the PR description. closing the loop after merge.
Emma: sweet, will mark demo as green.
